key_insight: Targeted continual pretraining on a large, curated cybersecurity corpus (11.8B tokens, 28.6K docs) yields a generalist LLM—RedSage—that better supports diverse security workflows while avoiding the privacy risks of proprietary APIs.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between privacy-risky proprietary LLM services and under-adapted open models by producing a domain-adapted, privacy-conscious cybersecurity language model for operations and tooling.
method: Large-scale data curation: filtered web scraping plus manual collection to assemble 11.8B tokens across 28.6K cybersecurity documents (frameworks, offensive techniques, tools).
Continual pretraining: adapt a foundation LLM on the curated cybersecurity corpus to create a generalist model specialized for security workflows.
Privacy-aware deployment emphasis: designed as an alternative to sending sensitive telemetry to proprietary APIs, enabling safer on-premise or self-hosted use.
impact: Enables AI/ML and security teams to use a specialized, privacy-conscious LLM for incident response, threat analysis, and tool integration—reducing dependence on closed APIs and improving domain relevance.
visual_elements: Data pipeline diagram: web filtering + manual collection → 11.8B tokens / 28.6K docs
